plugins.name: omx balancer
plugins.doc: Walks four bands slowly toward a target tone, so a mix settles toward a pink-noise balance without chasing notes.

plugins.name: omx chorus
plugins.doc: The console's chorus: up to four voices read one modulated delay line, the right leg's sweep offset by the spread, mixed with the dry signal.

plugins.name: omx clipper
plugins.doc: Clips the peaks at a ceiling, with drive in front and an adjustable softness of the bend.

plugins.name: omx comp
plugins.doc: The console's compressor: threshold, ratio and knee set how hard it holds the level down, attack and release how fast, with makeup gain and a dry/wet mix. Kind picks the RMS detector (Compressor) or the peak detector (Limiter), and detector oversampling can run the control path at 4x; detector topology has it hear the input (feedforward) or its own output (feedback). Its detector can listen to a key routed to its sidechain input instead, through a high-pass, a low-pass and a tilt, on the louder leg, the mid or the side, with a hold; key listen puts what the detector hears on the output, and duck holds the reduction to a set depth. The DSP is omx-dsp's <omxdsp/fx/omx_comp_instance.h>, the console's own compressor.

plugins.name: omx deesser
plugins.doc: The console's de-esser: a detector on a band around the sibilance drives the compressor's gain computer, and the reduction lands on that band alone or on the whole signal.

plugins.name: omx delay
plugins.doc: The OpenMixer console's stereo delay: one time, free or synced to the host's tempo, feedback through a tone filter, ping-pong, read taps, a tape or analog colour, a wet/dry mix and a duck under the input.

controls.name: Division
controls.values: 0 1/1, 1 1/1 dotted, 2 1/1 triplet, 3 1/2, 4 1/2 dotted, 5 1/2 triplet, 6 1/4, 7 1/4 dotted, 8 1/4 triplet, 9 1/8, 10 1/8 dotted, 11 1/8 triplet, 12 1/16, 13 1/16 dotted, 14 1/16 triplet, 15 1/32, 16 1/32 dotted, 17 1/32 triplet

plugins.name: omx doubler
plugins.doc: Doubles a voice or an instrument with up to four slightly delayed, detuned and drifting copies spread across the stereo field, the double-tracked sound without a second take.

plugins.name: omx drive
plugins.doc: The console's drive: one waveshaper (soft, tape, tube or exciter) run inside the console's oversampler, on the full band, the lows, the highs or a tilt, with a wet/dry mix and a trim.

plugins.name: omx ducker
plugins.doc: Pulls the programme down while a key is heard, music under a voice, by a set depth with attack, hold and release, the console ducker.

plugins.name: omx dyneq
plugins.doc: A six-band dynamic EQ: each band is an EQ bell or shelf whose gain also moves with the level of its own band, cutting above a threshold (down) or lifting below it (up), held to a range, so a harsh or boomy band is tamed only while it is too loud.

plugins.name: omx eq16
plugins.doc: The OpenMixer console's channel EQ, 16-band form: 16 parametric bands (bell, shelves, notch, all-pass) and a high-pass and a low-pass filter at 12 or 24 dB/oct, stereo, zero latency; every band ships off, so a racked instance is a wire.

plugins.name: omx eq32
plugins.doc: The OpenMixer console's channel EQ, 32-band form: 32 parametric bands (bell, shelves, notch, all-pass) and a high-pass and a low-pass filter at 12 or 24 dB/oct, stereo, zero latency; every band ships off, so a racked instance is a wire.

plugins.name: omx eq8
plugins.doc: The OpenMixer console's channel EQ, 8-band form: 8 parametric bands (bell, shelves, notch, all-pass) and a high-pass and a low-pass filter at 12 or 24 dB/oct, stereo, zero latency; every band ships off, so a racked instance is a wire.

plugins.name: omx flanger
plugins.doc: The console's flanger: one modulated short delay with signed feedback, swept by one oscillator and mixed with the dry signal.

plugins.name: omx geq
plugins.doc: The console's 31-band graphic EQ: one fader per ISO third-octave band from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, each cutting or boosting by up to 15 dB.

plugins.name: omx glue
plugins.doc: A bus compressor with the detents of a classic console: stepped ratio, attack and release, a key filter and a dry mix.

plugins.name: omx keyed-gate
plugins.doc: The OpenMixer console's channel gate with an external key: the stereo signal is gated while the detector listens to the sidechain input the host routes to it, or to the signal itself with the key unconnected or set to Self. One gain drives both legs. An attack under 0.5 ms engages 4x detector oversampling, which adds 72 frames of latency, reported to the host. The DSP is omx-dsp's <omxdsp/fx/omx_gate_instance.h>, the console's own gate.

plugins.name: omx limiter
plugins.doc: The precision limiter: a look-ahead, true-peak, stereo-linked brickwall.

plugins.name: omx loudlevel
plugins.doc: Holds a signal at a loudness target by moving its gain slowly, with a gate so pauses are left alone.

plugins.name: omx multiband
plugins.doc: A multiband compressor: two to five bands split by Linkwitz-Riley crossovers, each band its own compressor with threshold, ratio, attack, release, make-up, solo and bypass, then a mix and an output gain, for in-ear mixes, vocals and playback buses.

plugins.name: omx phaser
plugins.doc: The console's phaser: identical all-pass sections swept in octaves by one oscillator, with feedback around the chain and a wet/dry mix.

plugins.name: omx pitch
plugins.doc: The console's pitch shifter: shifts both channels up or down by semitones and cents, without changing their length, mixed with the dry signal.

plugins.name: omx plosive
plugins.doc: Softens the p pops and hard t and k consonants of a voice, cutting each only while it bursts.

plugins.name: omx reverb
plugins.doc: The console's reverb: room, plate, hall, reverse and gated algorithms with pre-delay, size, damping, width and low and high cuts, mixed with the dry signal; the early reflections and the tail set apart, the wet ducked under the dry and de-essed in its band.

plugins.name: omx rotary
plugins.doc: The console's rotary speaker: a drum rotor on the low band and a horn rotor on the high band, with stop, slow and fast speeds, mixed with the dry signal.

plugins.name: omx spring
plugins.doc: A spring reverb: a delay, a chain of all-passes and a darkening loop, with decay, length, tension and damping.

plugins.name: omx strip
plugins.doc: The OpenMixer console's channel strip in one plugin: input trim, high- and low-pass filters, gate, a parametric EQ of as many bands as its Bands control says, and compressor, in the console's order or any other. No DSP of its own: each stage is omx-dsp's instance face of the console's kernel, called in order.

plugins.name: omx suboct
plugins.doc: Adds a note one or two octaves below a single played line, by dividing its pitch, with a tracking range and a gate for quiet input.

plugins.name: omx tone
plugins.doc: Tilts the whole tone darker or brighter about a pivot, and sweeps a resonant DJ filter from a low-pass through open to a high-pass with one knob.

plugins.name: omx transient
plugins.doc: The console's transient designer: more or less attack and sustain, from two envelope contrasts, with no threshold to set.

plugins.name: omx tremolo
plugins.doc: The console's tremolo and auto-pan: one oscillator turned into a level change on both legs, or into a left-right pan.

plugins.name: omx trim
plugins.doc: The OpenMixer console's input trim: one gain control, -24 to +24 dB in 0.1 dB steps, applied first in the channel as a click-free ramp, stereo, zero latency; at 0 dB a racked instance is a wire.

plugins.name: omx upward
plugins.doc: Lifts what is quiet toward a threshold, by a ratio and up to a limit, and leaves the loud alone.

plugins.name: omx width
plugins.doc: Widens or narrows the stereo image, with an optional pseudo-stereo spread for a mono source and a bass-mono cutoff that keeps the lows centred.
